_note: Source of truth for the changelog page + guide footers; versions.json is re-derived from it. ADD RELEASES WITH: node scripts/add-release.mjs <track> <version> "Title" "note" [more notes] (--date=YYYY-MM-DD to backfill, --dry to preview). It prepends the entry and re-derives versions.json. Hand-edit only to fix an existing entry. Rules the script does not enforce, keep them yourself: ONLY add a version once it has actually deployed / published (not built-but-undeployed); one row per minor, fold same-day patch hotfixes into the minor's notes; notes stay capability-level (no formulas, estimator names, internal milestone codes, or PR numbers). Current per track = highest semver present, so a new release moves the prior current into history automatically. History reconciled 2026-08-16 against docs/team-rupert-signals + docs/compaction-reports; dates before 0.24.0 are approximate and cluster on sprint-close days.

releases.title: The judge's full light source
notes: Capture the judge's requested provider and credential beside its served model, so a judge change is attributed to the judge and not to your agent.
Vendor fan-out runs carry per-leg identity.
Richer health findings for judges and rubrics.

releases.title: Judge light source: attribution fix
notes: The judge's requested provider and credential now resolve correctly on live traffic.

releases.title: Know the judge's light source
notes: Capture the judge's requested provider and credential beside the model it actually served, so a change of judge is attributed to the judge and not mistaken for a change in your own agent.

releases.title: Holonograph enters beta
notes: The pre-launch hardening pass is complete: security, reliability, and scoring consistency are at production grade, and Holonograph is ready for beta use.
Scoring produces results identical to the prior release, so upgrading changes nothing you have already measured.

releases.title: Sharper refusal detection, honest health
notes: Wrongful-refusal detection along a conversation was tightened to flag only clear cases, so ordinary phrasing no longer trips a false alarm.
Lens Health shows a measuring state instead of a false none while a slow read completes, and its vendor readout lists every model in the window, not just the latest.

releases.title: A root-cause attention queue
notes: Findings now carry their prerequisites: a downstream flag is marked blocked and traced to the upstream cause, so you fix the root first.
A finding flags when a facet is scored on the default rubric because its own reference did not resolve, so you can point it at the intended one.
New health findings surface when judges or scoring axes overlap, disagree, or drift together, so a real signal is easier to tell from an instrument artifact.

releases.title: Grok joins the vendor lineup
notes: Run and compare xAI's Grok alongside your other model vendors, including side by side in a single run.
Current Google Gemini models are available again through their latest aliases.

releases.title: Dependable Explore filters
notes: The role filter now narrows the list itself, and internal records stay available even when you have scoped to a surface.
A malformed date can no longer wedge the dashboard: date inputs are validated and bounded.

releases.title: Readable evaluation rows
notes: Judge rows show a clean, title-cased name for what they grade, with the full identifier a hover away.
A surface's full description moves into its slide-over, and scoping to a judge reveals its events with an accurate count.

releases.title: Honest multiplex results
notes: Run one prompt across vendors and each leg now captures structured and tool-call output, and says plainly why any response is missing instead of a single catch-all.
Explore groups surfaces by role, refreshes on its own, and moves the lens's coverage and delivery records to their own opt-in.

releases.title: Rubrics that weigh contradiction, not silence
notes: A drafted rubric distinguishes a contradicted claim from one simply left unstated, so a partial answer is not penalized for what it did not address.

releases.title: Local-time stamps, cleaner Explore
notes: Clock times across the dashboard render in your local timezone, while calendar dates stay in UTC on purpose.
Explore tucks the lens's own evaluation runs behind an internal-records toggle, so your event stream reads as your traffic.

releases.title: Attested identity for your grading judge
notes: Declare your own grading judge and its identity is attested the same way the platform's judges are.

releases.title: Proposed rubrics ready to score
notes: The dimensions a de-saturation proposal drafts are registered so each one can be scored on its own.

releases.title: De-saturation, end to end
notes: The de-saturation proposal now runs its full loop cleanly, from detecting the saturated judge to drafting and delivering the sharper dimensions.

releases.title: Rescue a saturated judge
notes: When a judge stops distinguishing good from great and its scores collapse toward one value, the lens flags the saturation and proposes sharper rubric dimensions to restore resolution.

releases.title: Judges mapped to what they grade
notes: Declare which judge grades a dimension and the topology map nests that judge under the surface it drives, instead of drawing it as its own peak.
Judges no subject has claimed yet are grouped honestly as not yet linked.

releases.title: Lens Health without the wait
notes: Lens Health and the topology map open right away: readings are precomputed and served with an 'as of' time, with a manual refresh on demand.
Heavy recomputation runs off the request path, so the dashboard stays responsive.

releases.title: Coverage numbers you can trust
notes: Per-surface dimension counts and rubric pins now read from your live contract instead of showing zero.
The rubric-coverage card reflects your real coverage instead of reading empty when a check runs slow.

releases.title: Stable model identity across keys
notes: A per-credential routing change no longer reads as a model change: the model identity stays fixed while the key varies.

releases.title: Attested judge identity
notes: See which model, key, and rubric graded each result, with the lens's own record of whether it observed that identity or the scorer reported it.
Address one model through several credentials and track each one on its own.

releases.title: Several credentials per vendor
notes: Address a single vendor through several API credentials, so rate limits, billing, and attribution can be separated per agent or per key.
Each call records the credential that actually served it.

releases.title: Hardened service defaults
notes: Webhook targets aimed at an internal or cloud-metadata host are refused when you add them, not only when they fire.
Baseline security headers ship on every response, and a malformed request returns a clear error instead of a server fault.
Rate-limit headers report your remaining headroom on each request.

releases.title: Screen webhook targets before sending
notes: Check a webhook target for private or disguised network addresses in the client before you register it, using the same rule the lens enforces.

releases.title: Safer webhooks and steadier service
notes: Notification webhooks now refuse private or disguised network addresses, both when you set one up and each time it fires.
Encrypt a webhook's signing secret at rest with a single setup key.
Requests are rate limited so the service stays responsive under heavy load.

releases.title: Verdict-routing types
notes: Adds the wire types for verdict subscriptions and signed webhook payloads, and for the refined coverage and events reads.

releases.title: The reliability loop, front and center
notes: The README now leads with the verdict-reliability loop: attach a structured claim and the lens checks your judge for you.
Adds direction to a fabricated-datum claim and the judge-claim-coverage types.

releases.title: Structured judge claims
notes: reportOutcome forwards a structured judge claim, a value the judge says was fabricated or a tool it says was never called, for the lens to verify.
Exports the judge-claim and assertion types.

releases.title: Route a verdict to a human
notes: Route a lens verdict to an HMAC-signed webhook when a predicate over your own verdicts fires: a conformance fixture fails, a column that should always emit goes silent, or a dimension scores below a threshold.
Coverage now separates pre-instrumentation history from real gaps, so turning it on no longer reads as breakage.
The events read reports how many events the current provenance scope hid, so an empty result is never mistaken for a failed emit.

releases.title: See which verdicts you can trust
notes: A new read shows, per dimension, whether a judge claim was declared and emitted, so you can see how much of an evaluation is reliability-checked.
Rubric coverage in Lens Health now reflects the rubrics actually observed instead of a misleading zero.

releases.title: The honest instrument
notes: The reliability layer reads a structured claim from your judge instead of parsing prose, and checks it deterministically against the captured call.
Uninstrumented data stays honest-null rather than manufacturing a finding.
A new signal when a judge output is malformed, instead of silently trusting it.

releases.title: Report a judge for each dimension
notes: Attach a distinct judge identity to each dimension of an outcome, so an evaluation split across several focused judges records each one on its own rather than collapsing to a single judge.

releases.title: Faceted evaluation, tracked per judge
notes: Split one response across several focused judges and the lens groups and attributes each facet on its own, reporting where two move together rather than guessing which to credit.
Grounding checks respect the exact amount of context each judge saw, so a judge given a larger view is not flagged for reading something it was actually shown.

releases.title: Trace any event to its run
notes: Every event id across the dashboard is now readable and traceable: it shows the surface it belongs to, reveals the full id on hover, copies with a click, and links straight to that exact run in Explore.
Lens Health opens instantly: the panel, your surface list, and drift readout appear right away while the topology map fills in behind a progress indicator, instead of a long blank wait.
The topology map stays readable on large contracts: only the busiest surfaces are labelled, and you can hover any peak to reveal its full name.

releases.title: Live Lens Health at a glance
notes: The Lens Health summary in the header now shows your real numbers instead of placeholder values: pass rate, delivery reach, rubric coverage, and judge status.
Opening a missing-signal finding's evidence from the attention queue no longer errors.
The dashboard can now run embedded elsewhere in a clean, chrome-free dark view.

releases.title: A native math core
notes: The statistical core now runs on a native, accelerated engine. Every estimate is verified identical to the previous version, down to the last digit.
Entirely under the hood: the same numbers, computed faster and with the method better protected.

releases.title: Deeper drill evidence
notes: See which judge scored each cohort behind a hidden-factor finding, so a real difference is told apart from a judge that simply changed.
A signal you declared but whose surface has not run yet now reads 'cannot assess' instead of looking healthy.
When a declared column and the value you are actually sending are the same signal under two names, the lens suggests a rename rather than leaving a silent gap.
Every finding now tells you up front whether its evidence can be replayed or is too old to re-run.

releases.title: Sharper hidden-factor findings
notes: Hidden-factor findings now flag when the split really tracks calendar dates or a change of judge, not the factor itself.
The evidence drill shows examples from every group, so a lopsided comparison is obvious at a glance.
Resolving a finding now tells you when it no longer matches anything in the current queue.

releases.title: A clearer attention queue

Noisy, low-signal flags no longer crowd the top of the attention queue.
Drill a finding's evidence straight from its row, deep-link to lens health, and a topology map that stays readable on wide screens.
